chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Razi, from Abu Muhammad al-Razi, from Isma'il ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Leaning (in a state of idleness) in the mosque is the monasticism of the Arabs, and the believer's seat is his mosque, and his cell (place of worship) is his home.'

key_terms.رَهْبَانِيَّةُ: Monasticism (refering to the pre-Islamic Arab practice of secluded worship or idleness)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of leaning in the mosque and the believer's relationship with their home and mosque?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi places this narration in the chapter on the virtue of mosques to contrast pre-Islamic Arab idleness (Rahbaniyyah) with the active, communal piety of the believer. It establishes the mosque not merely as a prayer hall but as the believer's primary social and spiritual hub, while the home functions as a private sanctuary for contemplation. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing public religious engagement with private spiritual discipline.
